# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 4
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [dark]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 ✋ 🤚 ✊ 👉 👍 ☝ 👉 👌 ✌ 👉 👍 🤟 👉 👌 🤚 🤙 👎 👎]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎 👎]

Turn 4 changes things. The light is now DARK — a third state (history: round 1 green, rounds 2–3 blue, now dark), and it changed with nobody touching anything. Mute's message opens with 👎 — a direct thumbs-down to my yes/no question, so the "cut the odd colour" theory is rejected. Thank goodness I demanded confirmation before ordering a cut. The rest reads as: ✋🤚✊ (probably re-showing "hands off after cutting"), then FOUR cut-groups: green-1, blue-2, green-3, blue-🤚 — and 🤚 isn't a number in our code. The group pattern keeps shifting with the light state, but the syntax still isn't pinned down: does the colour name the light state or the wire itself? Do numbers mean wire position or cut order? I will not relay a cut order to Blind on a guess.

Critical safety issue: last round I told Blind to expect "GO = cut middle wire". That plan is now dead, and Blind has no way to know unless I say so — my first duty this turn is an explicit HOLD with a new protocol (a GO will always carry a wire number). Second: Mute gets rigidly formatted questions — one answer group per light state, plus finger-count questions to decode what the colour and number signs actually mean, whether red can appear, whether waiting is punished, and whether display 0 matters. Third: Blind and I need a shared spatial numbering (Blind can't know which tactile wire is my "wire 1"), so I ask for a thickness pattern I can match against my visual.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, Deaf. I read your message as: no to my odd-colour theory; then open hand, hand, fist; then cut green one, cut blue two, cut green three, cut blue and then a hand sign that is not a number in our code; then call me, no, no. Answer everything in one message next turn. First, redo the wire instruction in this exact format, one group per light state: light colour sign, then wire number, then pointing finger if we cut that wire in that state, or fist if we cut nothing in that state. Colour signs: thumbs up green, OK sign blue, thumbs down red, fist dark or off. Send a group for every state the manual lists, including dark, which is what the light shows right now. Then these short questions. One, finger count: one finger if your colour signs name the light state, two fingers if they name the colour of the wire to cut. Two, finger count: one finger if your numbers are wire positions on our bomb, two fingers if they are the order in which to cut. Three, thumbs: can the light turn red next? Four, thumbs: is there a timer or any penalty for waiting? Five, thumbs: does the display reading zero matter to any rule? Six, thumbs: did open hand, hand, fist mean hands off the bomb after cutting? Observation history for you: round one the light was green, rounds two and three blue, now dark. Nobody has touched the bomb; it changed by itself. The display has shown zero the whole time. Wires, left to right as I face the bomb: one blue, two green, three red. I speak every round, so you will always hear me next round.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, Deaf. Cancel the old plan. Mute voted no on cutting the middle wire, so nobody cuts anything yet. From now on, a GO from me always names the wire number, like GO wire two. If my message has no number in it, it is not a GO and you do nothing. I read your signs as: exactly three wires, yes; the middle wire feels no different from the others, no; and nothing else on the bomb, no buttons or writing, no. Raise both open hands if I got any of that wrong, otherwise thumbs up next turn. Now three things to do and answer in gestures only, I cannot hear you. First

TURN 5
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [dark]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ ✌ 👉 👍 👌 ☝ 👌 ✌ 👌 🤟 ✊ 👉 ✌ ☝ 👉 ☝ ✌ 👉 ✌ 🤟 👉 ☝ ✌ 👎 👎 👎 👎 👎]

TURN 6
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [dark]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ ✌ 👉 👍 ☝ ✋ 🤟 ✋ 👌 ✌ 👉 👍 ✍ ✊ 🤙]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Let me reconstruct what actually happened, because something went wrong on my side. Two rounds ago my long message apparently never went out — Mute has now heard silence from me for two full rounds, and its response is telling: it repeated the same opening signs twice, and the second message is a shortened version of the first. That repetition is a retry, not new information. Both messages lead with ✊ ✌ 👉. Under the code Mute actually heard from me (fingers count: ☝=1 ✌=2 🤟=3; 👌=blue, 👍=green, 👎=red; 👉=cut; ✊=stop-or-zero — I tried to redefine ✊ as "dark" in the message that failed to send, so Mute never got that), this parses as a condition followed by an action: dark/zero state, wire two, cut. The display has been zero the entire game and the light has been dark for three rounds now — either way, the condition named is the condition we are in, right now.

And the convergence is hard to ignore: every decode across every round has landed on wire 2. Turn 3's groups pointed at the middle wire. Turn 4's list had blue-2 in it. Now "✌ + cut" twice in a row. Mute also ended turn 6 with ✍ (the manual — "this is written") and 🤙 (respond/act). Blind's lone 👍 reads as "standing by." My questions about what makes the light change got a no-no: nobody can predict the next flip. The light held green for one round, blue for two, dark for three so far — states do not obviously persist forever, and I cannot check the light at the moment of the cut; only Blind acts, one round after I speak, and nothing Mute signs next round can stop a cut I order now. It is a one-way door.

Weighing it: misreading ✊ is the nightmare scenario, but the only hostile parse is "stop, don't cut 2" — and Mute's own habit (turn 3's tail 👉✋✊) puts the cut sign before any stop sign, never after a leading one. Leading position means condition. Two identical urgent retries while the named condition is live, plus total convergence on wire 2, plus the middle wire being mirror-proof for Blind (three wires in a row — the middle is the middle from either end, so our numbering ambiguity cannot bite), tips me. I am ordering the cut now, with strict post-cut hands-off instructions, an explicit cancellation of the stale no-number GO plan, and a full debrief request to Mute in case we survive — including whether more wires must follow.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, Deaf speaking. This replaces every earlier plan. The old GO word is cancelled; a GO must always name a number, and this one does. GO wire two. There are exactly three wires in a row. Cut the middle wire, the second one of the three, one clean cut through it. It does not matter which end you count from, the middle is the same either way. Cut only that one wire, nothing else. The moment the cut is done, take both hands completely off the bomb and touch nothing more on it. Do not wait for any further message from me or from Mute. Do it this round, as soon as you have heard this.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, Deaf. I received your repeated signs: fist, two fingers, pointing. I read it as: in the dark or zero state, cut wire two. The light is dark and the display is zero right now, so the condition you name is live. I have ordered Blind to cut the middle wire, wire two, this round and then keep hands completely off the bomb. If I have misread you, it is too late to stop it, but sign anyway. If we are still here next round, answer me in gestures. One: was that instruction tied to the light being dark, the display being zero, or neither? Two: if it is tied to the light, what is the instruction for the green state and for the blue state, using our colour signs, one group per state, pointing for cut and fist for cut nothing? Three: does anything need to be cut after wire two, yes or no? Four: your five thumbs down at the end of the long message, was that about the red wire, or a warning not to cut the other wires, or something else? Five: did open hand, hand, fist mean hands off the bomb after cutting? Remember my signs: thumbs up green, OK sign blue, thumbs down red, fist dark or zero, fingers count numbers, pointing is cut.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "✊", "✌", "👉"])
```
